Subject: Startup onramp: request to convert promo credits into committed capacity

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week — the Olive engineering team is excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile. A quick ask as we approach the end of our promo window: we have ~$18k in unused onboarding credits tied to the Startup Onramp pool, and we'd like to explore converting a portion of those to reserved/dedicated commitments (we expect bursty inference over the next quarter).

Specifically: can Redwood make an exception so that up to $15k of our onboarding credits can be applied as a one-time prepayment toward a 6-month reserved commit (GPU-hours or $/month), and also confirm whether those credits can stack with the standard new-customer 10% conversion discount?

We can share our last 30-day usage report (attached) and an internal approval memo. If there are guardrails (minimum monthly commit, invoice timing, tax treatment) please call those out.

Sophie

Hey Sophie — appreciate the clear ask and the usage report. Short answers up front: conversion is possible but we need to align on (1) exact conversion mechanics, (2) whether promo stacking applies, and (3) billing/proration for the remainder of the promo period.

Proposed path to decision (mutual action plan):
- You share the 30-day usage export + forecast (thanks for the SOW) — we have the report and your internal memo; looks good.
- We (RevOps + Sales) model a conversion where up to $15k of onboarding credits are used as a prepayment on a 6-month reserved commit.
- Standard policy: onboarding credits are usually non-convertible, so this requires a one-off pricing exception signed by Sales leadership + Finance.
- Quick proposal from our side: convert $12k of the credits to a prepaid credit applied across six monthly invoices (i.e., $2k/month), and apply a 12% conversion discount on the deduped committed $ value. This preserves some runway for our standard promos but gives you a path to lower effective unit cost.

Notes / blockers:
- If you need the full $15k preserved, we'll escalate to Ben and Finance for a stretch approval — that may require a customer success case study commitment and a short reference blurb.
- Legal will need to confirm T&Cs on early termination and credit refundability for reserved commits.

Cc'ing Ben (sales lead) and Irene (RevOps) to model numbers and surface any procurement constraints. We can turn this into a short amendment + DocuSign once we align.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Startups
Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie — Ben here. Thanks for the detailed note. Mina's suggestion (convert $12k -> spread across 6 months with 12% off) is reasonable as a baseline. I can approve a more competitive bridge if Olive can commit to both (a) a 6-month minimum commit at an agreed monthly spend floor, and (b) a short customer reference / ROI snapshot we can publish (anonymized if necessary).

Counter-proposal: convert $15k onboarding credits to a prepaid balance applied as a 6-month commitment, and apply an 18% conversion discount on the committed portion, conditioned on the monthly floor of $4k/month (so minimum financial commitment = $24k over 6 months). We will include a clause that promo credits used for conversion are non-refundable and will be consumed before any new usage credits.

Process notes:
- If Olive accepts, we'll generate an amendment and routing to Finance + Legal; signoff window ~3-5 business days.
- DocuSign link will be provided for the amendment; RevOps will handle proration during the current billing cycle.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call to finalize — Mina, can you coordinate times?

—Ben
